text: About 2,900 years ago, the Etruscans began to build their world in central Italy.
They built cities such as Veii and Tarquinia, and each city ruled itself.
src: The Etruscans of central Italy built rich, independent city-states from about 900 BCE / Etruria, between the Arno and the Tiber in central Italy
The Etruscans of central Italy built independent city-states such as Veii, Tarquinia, Caere and Vulci / Its cities ... were independent, each ruling its own territory

text: They grew rich from metals, farming and trade, and princes were buried with gold and ivory.
src: Wealth from metals, farming and trade created an aristocracy whose princely tombs ... were filled with gold, silver, bronze and ivory

text: Etruscan women had a freedom that surprised the Greeks and Romans.
They lay beside their husbands at feasts, like the couple on this tomb.
src: Etruscan women enjoyed a freedom that surprised Greek and Roman observers
They reclined beside their husbands at banquets, as on the Sarcophagus of the Spouses from Caere

text: Priests studied the livers of sheep to learn what the gods wanted.
This bronze model of a liver is marked with the names of gods.
src: The priests called haruspices read the will of the gods in the livers of sacrificed sheep
A bronze model of a liver found near Piacenza ... is divided into regions inscribed with the names of gods

text: Their language was unlike Latin or Greek, but its letters came from the Greeks.
These gold tablets from a port where they traded are written in both Etruscan and Phoenician.
src: They spoke a language unrelated to Latin or Greek, wrote it in an alphabet taken from the Greeks
At Pyrgi, the port of Caere, gold tablets of about 500 BCE record in Etruscan and Phoenician a dedication

text: Rome, their neighbour, conquered the Etruscan cities one by one, and their people became Romans.
We still have their painted tombs and their bronzes, like this Chimera from Arezzo.
src: Rome conquered Etruria city by city and absorbed its people in the 1st century BCE
are known above all from their tombs, with wall paintings, sculpture and rich grave goods / The Chimera of Arezzo ... among the finest ancient bronzes of Italy
